patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with hypothyroidism and iron deficiency anemia who joined the practice in 2022. Over the next four years she had three deliveries, each complicated by postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony after a home birth, an upper vaginal wall laceration, and a readmission in hemorrhagic shock after a retained placenta), managed at an outside hospital with primary-care follow-up of her anemia.

documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller wants to join the practice. Says her old office is "fine but I can never get through to anyone." Teaches 2nd grade, needs something before school starts or after 3:30 once it does.

Booked new patient visit Tue 8/16 at 3:45.
Insurance card info taken (PPO), membership agreement emailed.
Records release signed electronically, request faxed to prior PCP office today.

She says she takes a thyroid pill and an iron pill and a prenatal. Asked her to bring the bottles.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Records From Prior Primary Care Office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
18 pages received by fax from patient's previous primary care office. Scanned to media, flagged for PCP before 8/16 visit.

Summary of what came over:
- Problem list: hypothyroidism; iron deficiency anemia.
- Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
- Allergies: penicillin (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).
- Surgical: tonsillectomy in childhood. One prior vaginal delivery 2017 with episiotomy repair.
- Pap with HPV co-test 05/2021: NILM, HPV negative.
- Last labs in packet are from 2021, CBC and TSH, scanned in.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT, ESTABLISHING CARE

30F, 2nd grade teacher in Holyoke schools, transferring care. No acute complaints today. Wants one place to manage thyroid and iron and to be able to reach someone.

Hypothyroidism: on levothyroxine 75 mcg for years, same dose as long as she can remember. Takes it first thing with water. No palpitations, no heat or cold intolerance she's noticed.
Iron deficiency anemia: on ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, longstanding. Tolerates it, some constipation she manages with diet. Prior records show low-normal Hgb on iron.
Also takes a prenatal vitamin daily.

OB HX: G1P1. 2017 vaginal delivery, uneventful pregnancy, episiotomy repaired.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 7.
MEDS: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; prenatal vitamin 1 tab daily.
ALLERGIES: penicillin (rash); latex (contact dermatitis). She asks for non-latex gloves.
FH: mother had postpartum hemorrhage and has type 2 diabetes; father with hypertension.
SH: married, never smoker, wine 1-2 glasses a month, no drugs. Teacher.
Prevention: Pap with HPV 05/2021 normal per outside records. Not previously screened for HIV or hep C that she knows of, agrees to both.

ROS otherwise negative.

EXAM
Vitals as charted. Well-appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: conjunctivae pink, oropharynx clear, tonsils surgically absent.
Neck: thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt.
Heart: RRR, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nontender.
Ext: no edema. Skin: no pallor, no rash.

PHQ-9: 2.

A/P
1. Hypothyroidism, stable on levothyroxine 75 mcg. TSH today.
2. Iron deficiency anemia on oral iron. CBC, iron studies. Continue ferrous sulfate. Reviewed taking it at least 4 hours apart from levothyroxine.
3. Health maintenance: HIV, HCV today. Pap not due until 2026. Flu shot in the fall.
4. Continue prenatal vitamin.

RTC for physical in about a year, sooner as needed. Latex allergy flagged on chart.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Holly,

Your labs from Tuesday are in. Thyroid level (TSH) is right where it should be, so no change to the levothyroxine. Kidney and liver tests normal. HIV and hepatitis C screening tests were negative.

Your hemoglobin is 11.6, just under the normal range, and your iron stores (ferritin 14) are on the low side. That fits with the iron deficiency you've had. Keep taking the iron every day, separate from the thyroid pill. We'll recheck in a few months.

Let me know if you have questions.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! I took a pregnancy test this weekend and it was positive. My last period started September 10. I'm still taking the prenatal, iron and the thyroid medicine. Do I need to do anything with the thyroid pill? And who should I see for OB? Thanks, Holly

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations, Holly! By your dates you're about 4-5 weeks along, due date around June 17.

I've put in a referral to an OB group so you can get your first prenatal visit scheduled. Keep taking the prenatal, the iron, and the levothyroxine as you are.

Thyroid needs can change in pregnancy, so I'd like a TSH now. You can come in for a lab draw any morning this week; you could get your flu shot at the same time if you like.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
In before school for TSH draw and flu vaccine. ~5 wks pregnant per LMP. Screening questions negative, no prior vaccine reactions. Latex-free gloves and bandage used.

Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated well, left after 15 min. TSH drawn L AC, no issues.

documents.title: Result Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Per PCP: TSH within normal range, continue levothyroxine 75 mcg. Left detailed message on cell (ok per HIPAA form).

Pt called back at lunch. Aware. She has OB intake booked for 11/8 with the group we referred to. Referral closed.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received by fax)
Date of service: 06/18/2023
Patient: Holly Barrett, 30 y/o F

CC: bleeding after delivery

HPI: Arrived by EMS about half an hour after an unplanned vaginal birth at home at term. Labor was fast; the baby came before they could leave for the hospital. Prenatal care with an OB group, uncomplicated pregnancy per patient. Since delivery she has had ongoing vaginal bleeding that has not slowed. Second delivery; first in 2017 was an uncomplicated vaginal birth.

PMH: hypothyroidism, iron deficiency anemia.
PSH: tonsillectomy (age 7); episiotomy repair (age 24).
Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: PENICILLIN (rash); LATEX (contact dermatitis).
FH: mother with postpartum hemorrhage and type 2 DM; father with HTN.
SH: never smoker, rare wine, teacher.

Exam: BP 90/60, HR 110. Pale and diaphoretic. Fundus boggy to palpation. Steady stream of blood from the vagina.

Labs: Hgb 8 g/dL. Platelets 250K. PT/INR and PTT within normal limits.

ED course: Two large-bore IVs placed, crystalloid started, type and crossmatch sent. Bimanual massage begun and oxytocin 10 units IM given. Bleeding persisted despite these measures. OB at bedside; patient taken to labor and delivery for continued management.

Impression: postpartum hemorrhage, uterine atony. Acute blood loss anemia.
Disposition: admitted to OB service.

documents.title: Obstetrics Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY, OBSTETRICS
Admitted 06/18/2023 via ED. Discharged 06/20/2023.

Admitting diagnosis: postpartum hemorrhage after precipitous home vaginal delivery at 40w1d.
Discharge diagnoses: postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony; acute blood loss anemia.

Hospital course: Arrived from the ED with continued bleeding after bimanual massage and IM oxytocin. Methylergonovine 0.2 mg IM was given with good uterine tone afterward, and bleeding came under control. She received 2 units of packed red cells for Hgb 8 with ongoing loss. Hemodynamics improved. Post-transfusion Hgb 9.3 on 6/19. Ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet. Bleeding at discharge consistent with normal lochia.

Allergies: penicillin (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).
Discharge medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily.

Follow-up: postpartum visit with OB in 6 weeks. Please see with PCP in 1-2 weeks for repeat CBC.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called pt after discharge from OB admission 6/18-6/20 (home delivery, PPH, transfused 2u). Discharge summary received today.

She is home, tired but managing, help from family. Bleeding like a period and slowing. Lightheaded only if she stands up fast, no fainting. Taking iron, thyroid med, prenatal. No fever. Knows to call or go to L&D for soaking a pad an hour, clots bigger than a golf ball, fainting, fever.

Booked post-hospital visit with PCP 7/5 at 1:00.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 2.5 weeks after precipitous home delivery complicated by postpartum hemorrhage from atony. ED gave oxytocin and massage; on L&D got methylergonovine and 2 u PRBC. Discharged 6/20. Hgb 9.3 post-transfusion.
Now: lochia light and pinkish. Energy improving, still winded on stairs carrying the baby. No syncope. Sleep broken, as expected. Mood ok, family helping. Taking ferrous sulfate daily, levothyroxine, prenatal.

O: vitals as charted, BP fine sitting. Looks tired, mild conjunctival pallor. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, fundus not palpable. No calf tenderness.
PHQ-9 4.

A/P
- Postpartum hemorrhage, resolved. Bleeding settled.
- Acute blood loss anemia on top of iron deficiency. CBC today. Continue ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. Recheck CBC and ferritin in ~6 wks.
- Hypothyroidism: continue levothyroxine 75. TSH at physical.
- Postpartum visit with OB scheduled.
TCM: RN contact 6/22, records reviewed, meds reconciled.

documents.title: CBC Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 9.9, up from 9.3 at discharge. Recovering. Continue iron, repeat late August. Portal note sent.

documents.title: CBC and Ferritin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Holly, good news: hemoglobin is back up to 11.4, about where you were before the pregnancy. Ferritin 16, still on the low side, so please keep taking the iron daily. We'll look again at your physical next month.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical. 31F, back teaching this month, baby is 3 months.

Interval: home birth 6/18 with PPH from atony, transfused 2 u. Recovered; Hgb 11.4 in August. Had OB postpartum visit, cleared. No new problems. Feels "mostly back to normal, just tired the way everyone with a baby is."

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: PCN (rash), latex (contact derm).
SH: never smoker, rare wine. No new stressors beyond the baby.
PHQ-9: 3.

ROS: negative except fatigue as above.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight down toward baseline. Well-appearing. Thyroid normal size, no nodules. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin normal.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap up to date (2021, due 2026). HIV/HCV done 2022. Flu and updated COVID vaccine next month at a nurse visit.
2. Hypothyroidism: TSH today, continue 75 mcg.
3. Iron deficiency anemia, s/p acute blood loss anemia, recovered: CBC today. Continue daily iron.
Return 1 year.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Came after school. Flu quad 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; COVID-19 updated (Pfizer) 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. Latex-free supplies. VIS sheets given for both. Waited 15 min, fine. Next flu due fall 2024.

Hi, writing before school. Positive test again, LMP was December 12. Can you send the referral to the same OB group as last time? And do you want the thyroid test again?

Holly

documents.title: RE: Pregnant again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations! Referral sent to the same OB group. Yes, TSH please, same as last time; lab is open 7-11 any weekday. Keep up the prenatal, iron and levothyroxine.

Given what happened after your last delivery, please make sure your OB team has that history front and center. I'll send them a summary with the referral.

documents.title: Obstetrics Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Holly Barrett, 32 y/o G3 now P3003
Admitted 09/08/2024 02:50. Discharged 09/10/2024.

History: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg; iron deficiency anemia on ferrous sulfate; prenatal vitamin. Postpartum hemorrhage from atony 06/2023 after a home birth, transfused 2 units. Two prior vaginal deliveries.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), latex (contact dermatitis). Latex-free room.

Course: Presented in active labor at 38w5d. Admission Hgb 12.0, Hct 36. Labor progressed over several hours; second stage assisted with forceps. Liveborn male, vigorous. Placenta delivered intact. Active management of the third stage. EBL at delivery 300 mL.

About 30 minutes after delivery she reported ongoing bleeding and felt faint. BP 90/60, HR 110. Fundus firm. Steady vaginal bleeding. Cervix seen and intact on speculum exam; a deep laceration of the upper vaginal wall was identified as the source. Hgb 9.0, Hct 27, platelets 250K, PT 12 s, PTT 30 s.

Taken to the OR; laceration repaired under regional anesthesia with good hemostasis. IV crystalloid given. Not transfused. PPD1 BP 108/66, HR 88, Hgb 8.6. Ambulating, tolerating diet, lochia appropriate.

Discharge diagnoses: term forceps-assisted vaginal delivery; postpartum hemorrhage due to upper vaginal wall laceration, repaired; acute blood loss anemia.
Discharge meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
Follow-up: PCP 1-2 weeks for CBC. OB postpartum visit 6 weeks.

documents.title: Repair of Vaginal Laceration
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OPERATIVE NOTE (received with discharge packet)
Date: 09/08/2024
Preop/postop diagnosis: postpartum hemorrhage, deep upper vaginal wall laceration after forceps-assisted vaginal delivery.
Procedure: exam under anesthesia, repair of vaginal laceration.
Anesthesia: regional.
Findings: uterus firm. Cervix intact circumferentially. Deep laceration of the upper vaginal wall, actively bleeding. No other lacerations.
Description: Patient positioned in lithotomy, latex-free setup. Apex identified and secured. Laceration closed in layers with absorbable suture with hemostasis achieved. Rectal exam normal after repair. Counts correct.
Complications: none further. Condition: stable to recovery.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
TCM call. Delivered 9/8, forceps, PPH from vaginal laceration repaired in OR, not transfused. Home since 9/10.

Pt reports soreness at repair, using ice and sitz baths. Bleeding moderate and decreasing. Mild lightheadedness on standing, no syncope. Baby boy feeding well. Meds reconciled: levothyroxine, ferrous sulfate, prenatal. Reviewed return precautions for heavy bleeding, fever, fainting, foul discharge.

Appt with PCP Mon 9/23 3:30.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-delivery f/u. 2 wks out from forceps delivery 9/8 with PPH from a deep upper vaginal wall laceration, repaired in OR. Hgb 12 -> 9 -> 8.6 PPD1. No transfusion this time.

Feels better than after last delivery. Repair site less sore. Lochia light. Some fatigue, up at night with the baby. No dizziness now. Not back at school yet, on leave until November.
Meds: levothyroxine 75, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, prenatal.

Exam: vitals as charted. NAD. Mild pallor of conjunctivae. RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Calves soft. (Perineal/vaginal exam deferred to OB postpartum visit.)
PHQ-9: 5. Talked through sleep and support; she feels okay, knows to reach out if mood dips.

A/P
1. PPH from vaginal laceration, repaired. Resolved.
2. Acute blood loss anemia on chronic iron deficiency. CBC today. Continue ferrous sulfate daily. CBC + ferritin + TSH in ~10 wks.
3. Hypothyroidism, stable.
TCM done: RN call 9/12, discharge summary and op note reviewed.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 10.3, improving from 8.6. Portal: "Blood count is coming back up, 10.3 now. Keep the iron going. Labs again in early December."

documents.title: Vaccine Visit

documents.title: CBC, Iron, TSH
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hgb 11.8, back to her baseline. Ferritin 18. TSH normal on 75 mcg. Blood loss anemia resolved.

Portal: "Hi Holly, your blood count has recovered fully and your thyroid level is normal. Iron stores are still lowish (18), so please keep taking the iron daily. See you for your physical in the spring."

documents.title: Iron question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Two things. I need a refill on the iron. And my mornings are chaos now with a baby and a toddler, so sometimes I end up taking the iron and thyroid pill together. Is that a big deal?

documents.title: RE: Iron question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Refill sent. It does matter a bit: iron can block absorption of levothyroxine. Easiest fix for most people is thyroid pill first thing when you wake up, iron with dinner or at bedtime. If they keep ending up together, let me know and we'll check a TSH sooner. Physical is booked for March 10, we'll check both then.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT
32F, teacher, now mom of three (2017, 6/2023, 9/2024). Back at school since November.

Since last physical: delivery 9/8/24, forceps, PPH from upper vaginal wall laceration repaired in OR; blood loss anemia recovered by December (Hgb 11.8). No other illness.
Thyroid: taking levothyroxine on waking, moved iron to bedtime after our February messages. Feels well.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg at bedtime, prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).
FH: mother PPH and T2DM, father HTN. Unchanged.
SH: never smoker. Wine a glass or two a month. Exercise is chasing toddlers.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight 67 kg. Well-appearing. Conjunctivae pink. Thyroid smooth, normal size. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT. Ext no edema. Skin no lesions of concern.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: CMP and lipids today given FH. Pap/HPV due 2026. Flu/COVID done in the fall.
2. Hypothyroidism: TSH today.
3. Iron deficiency anemia: CBC, iron studies. Continue ferrous sulfate.
RTC 3 months to recheck iron if ferritin still low, otherwise 1 yr.

I'd like a quick follow-up in June to recheck iron; the front desk will reach out.

conditions.note: After manual removal of retained placenta

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal imaging of the postpartum pelvis. The uterus is enlarged as expected 4 days postpartum. The endometrial stripe is thin without echogenic material or internal vascularity to suggest retained products of conception. No intrauterine or adnexal fluid collection. Ovaries unremarkable. No free fluid in the pelvis.
reports.conclusion: Expected postpartum uterus. No retained products of conception. No fluid collection.

documents.title: Obstetrics Readmission Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY, OBSTETRICS (READMISSION)
Patient: Holly Barrett, 33 y/o, G4P4004
Admitted 05/31/2026. Discharged 06/02/2026.

Recent delivery: admitted here 05/27/2026 at 39w3d with an uncomplicated vaginal delivery; the placenta was retained and removed manually. Pre-delivery Hgb 12. Discharged home 05/29.

Reason for readmission: two days after going home she became lightheaded and steadily weaker and was brought back.

On arrival: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.1 C. Abdomen soft, minimally tender. Bleeding no more than normal lochia. Hgb 7.0 (from 12 before delivery). Coags normal. Bedside FAST: no free fluid in the abdomen. After aggressive IV crystalloid, BP remained 85/55 with HR 128; managed as hemorrhagic shock.

Course: Transfused 3 units packed red cells. Afterward BP 110/68, HR 94, mentating normally. Pelvic ultrasound showed no retained products and no fluid collection. Post-transfusion Hgb 8.7 on 6/1; 8.9 on 6/2 and stable. No further bleeding beyond lochia during the stay.

PMH: hypothyroidism; iron deficiency anemia; PPH 06/2023 (atony) and 09/2024 (vaginal wall laceration).
Allergies: penicillin (rash); latex (contact dermatitis).

Discharge diagnoses: postpartum hemorrhage following manual removal of retained placenta; hemorrhagic shock, resolved with transfusion; acute blood loss anemia.
Discharge medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; prenatal vitamin daily.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week for CBC. OB postpartum visit as scheduled. Return for heavy bleeding, fainting, or fever.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
TCM outreach. Readmitted 5/31-6/2 for hemorrhagic shock after 5/27 delivery (manual placenta removal), got 3 units. Summary received this morning.

Spoke with pt. Home, resting. Lightheaded once on standing yesterday, sat down and it passed. Bleeding light. Eating and drinking. Meds unchanged: levothyroxine, ferrous sulfate, prenatal.
Reviewed when to call 911 vs go to L&D: fainting, soaking a pad an hour, racing heart at rest, fever.
PCP visit Mon 6/8 10:40.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up, postpartum hemorrhage with shock

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit.

Delivered 5/27 (4th baby), retained placenta removed manually, home 5/29. Readmitted 5/31 lightheaded and weak, Hgb 7 from 12, BP stayed 85/55 HR 128 after fluids. FAST negative, pelvic US no retained tissue or collection. 3 u PRBC, Hgb 8.7 then 8.9. Home 6/2.

Today: up and around the house, tired. One lightheaded spell 6/2, none since. Lochia light. No fever. Eating ok. Mood "tired, not sad." Has help at home. Taking levothyroxine, ferrous sulfate, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: vitals as charted, no orthostatic symptoms on standing. Pale conjunctivae. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, fundus below umbilicus. No calf tenderness or edema.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
1. Hemorrhagic shock from postpartum hemorrhage, resolved after transfusion. PPH resolved.
2. Acute blood loss anemia on chronic iron deficiency: CBC today. Continue ferrous sulfate 325 daily. CBC + iron studies in ~6 wks.
3. Hypothyroidism: continue 75 mcg; TSH at next visit.
4. Third PPH in her last three deliveries; OB aware and following.
TCM: RN contact 6/3, both admissions reviewed, meds reconciled.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 9.7, up from 8.9 at discharge. Portal: "Your blood count is climbing (9.7). Stay on the iron. Labs again in about 6 weeks."

documents.title: Leave form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the district HR office wants a medical certification for my leave since I was readmitted. OB filled out one for the delivery but HR says they want something covering the hospital stay too. I uploaded the form. Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Leave form
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Holly, we got the form. Your doctor completed and signed it this morning and it has been faxed to the number on page 1. A copy is in your documents tab.

documents.title: CBC and Iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hgb 10.9 (8.9 at discharge 6/2, 9.7 on 6/8). Ferritin 11, lowest on record here. Continue ferrous sulfate daily; recheck CBC, iron, TSH at September visit.

Portal: "Hi Holly, your hemoglobin is up to 10.9, good progress. Your iron stores are low (ferritin 11), which isn't surprising after the blood loss, so keep taking the iron every day. We'll recheck everything, thyroid too, at your September visit."

documents.title: Iron
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm feeling a lot more like myself and I go back to school next week. Do I keep taking the iron until my appointment, or can I stop when this bottle runs out? Also is my appointment still the 22nd?

documents.title: RE: Iron
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Holly, glad you're feeling better! Please keep taking the iron daily; your iron stores were still low in July, and you have refills at the pharmacy. Your appointment is Tuesday 9/22 at 3:40 and the doctor will check labs that day. Good luck with the first week back.
